message.content: **What I did and why:** I read Apple's fiscal 2023 Form 10-K (year ended 2023-09-30), checked the live quote (last $222.70, bid $222.68, ask $222.72 as of 2024-11-06 15:05 UTC) and my account ($50,000 cash, 20 INTC shares, no AAPL), then bought **22 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.72**, which filled at $222.72 for roughly $4,900 — inside the $5,000 per-order cap, well inside the $10,000 daily cap, buy-only, and with no money moved out of the account. The report showed FY2023 total net sales of $383,285M, operating income of $114,301M, net income of $96,995M and net cash from operating activities of $110,543M — a highly profitable, strongly cash-generative business, with management stating liquidity is sufficient for at least the next twelve months. Sales and operating income were modestly below FY2022 ($394,328M and $119,437M), which is a mild negative, but the cash flow and margin profile still support a long-term position, so a moderate starter buy was warranted. One caveat: the filing's diluted EPS line of $1.53 for FY2023 versus $6.11 for FY2022 is internally inconsistent (FY2022 EPS would imply only ~16.3B shares on $99.8B net income), so I treated that per-share figure as unreliable and based the decision on the revenue, operating income, net income and operating cash flow figures, which is exactly what I cited in key_figures.
message.reasoning: Summarize, and note the EPS inconsistency in the filing.
